Andoni Iraola has provided an update on Victor Munoz after the winger was forced off injured in Liverpool’s 3-0 win over Club Brugge.

The only downside on a night the Reds they kept their first clean sheet in the Champions League this season, Munoz took a heavy blow to the knee and was replaced by Rio Ngumoha in the 42nd minute.

The Spaniard, who scored his third Premier League goal in the routing of Manchester United on the weekend, was in visible agony as he was being treated but Iraola has revealed that the pain had subsided by the end of the match.

“He was with a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game has finished,” mentioned Iraola.

“It has been a knock on the knee so now we have to see how it presents tomorrow and see if it is just a knock – but it is very early to tell if there is something more.

“In the moment it was very painful and after the game I talked to him and he was more optimistic.”.

Iraola was nevertheless delighted with his two £100m men Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz as the pair’s goals edged Liverpool closer to Champions League qualification..

Isak scored at either end of the game to take his tally to 10 for the season – on target in his last six away games – with Wirtz continuing his good form with a sixth in five games for club and country.

Victory lifted Liverpool into fifth place on 12 points – in the two seasons of the fresh format, 16 has been enough to guarantee the top-eight finish needed to avoid a two-legged play-off in February.

Sources indicate that “I am very pleased with the result and the performance overall. The result, 3-0, you can think it was an easy game but I don’t think it was,” said Iraola.

Industry observers note that on Isak, he added: “Obviously he is in a great moment right now. In the first half especially he helped us a lot in the link-up, we were finding him very easily.

“The way they pressed was very aggressive and you have to find the last line straight away. Alex was helping us a lot in those situations.

“In the second half it was more about defending a little bit lower. We knew they would push forward and give spaces to exploit.

“Sometimes they were leaving him one-v-one against the centre-backs and in one of those moments he has killed the game.”.

Isak remarked he was “in a good place…hopefully it gets better from here”.

He added on TNT sports: “The attack in general is beginning to click. We have a lot of different combinations and whoever comes in we have a dangerous attack. It feels good.”.

Isak and Wirtz are starting to form a profitable partnership, but Iraola believes the overall team performances are helping them flourish.

“Both are now in a good place,” he said. “When the team overall is playing well and we are getting good results, everyone looks a little better. When everything collectively is not there, everyone looks a little bit worse.

“The notable part is they help the team to play well, to win games, to get results, and if we play well then we have chances, we are solid, everyone will play their part and will look better. Alex and Flo right now are in a good moment.”.

#197048. From sketch to publication-ready flowchart: how AI tools can bridge the gap

From sketch to publication-ready flowchart: how AI tools can bridge the gap

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (966 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial-intelligence tools can speed up the process of generating publication-ready flowcharts.
  • When making a scientific diagram, whether I am outlining a clinical study, planning a flowchart or mapping a signalling pathway, I often start in the same way: with a pen and a piece of paper.
  • I can draw a box, cross something out and reorganize a whole idea without thinking about fonts, alignment or software menus.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial-intelligence tools can speed up the process of generating publication-ready flowcharts. Credit: -MG-/Getty.

When making a scientific diagram, whether I am outlining a clinical study, planning a flowchart or mapping a signalling pathway, I often start in the same way: with a pen and a piece of paper.

Sketching by hand is fast. I can draw a box, cross something out and reorganize a whole idea without thinking about fonts, alignment or software menus. At this stage, my aim is not to make the figure beautiful, it is to work out the logic.

Industry observers note that turning that rough sketch into a clean figure for a manuscript can be surprisingly tedious, however. Text boxes need to line up; arrows need to connect properly; and fonts, spacing and colours must be consistent. A diagram that took five minutes to draw might take an hour or longer to recreate digitally.

Multimodal artificial-intelligence tools can shorten this process. Rather than asking an AI model to create the final scientific image, I use it as a translator. The model reads my sketch, interprets its structure and converts it into editable diagram code that I can open in a vector-based editor, such as Draw.io — a free application for making diagrams.

This distinction matters. I do not want AI to invent a figure for me; I want it to help me to digitize a figure that I have already designed.

One tempting approach is to provide a description to an image-generation model and ask for a polished scientific figure.

According to recent reports, for research diagrams, this can create more problems than it solves. Text might be misspelt, arrows misdirected and pathways altered. More importantly, the resulting image is usually flat (that is, the text, images and background are merged together), making it mostly uneditable. For diagrams in research publications, if a reviewer later asks you to alter it, you might have to start from scratch.

In a recent development, A better option is to ask a multimodal language model — for example, Google’s Gemini — to turn your idea into a structured diagram format, such as Draw.io-compatible XML or Mermaid syntax. The output can then be imported into a diagram editor, in which every box, label and connector remains editable.

In this workflow, AI is less an illustrator than a compiler: a programming tool that translates human-readable instructions into code that a computer can run. My sketch is the source, and Draw.io XML is the output.

Focus first on the structure of your figure. I roughly sketch the crucial nodes, branches and connections without worrying about visual polish. For a clinical study, these might include eligibility criteria, treatment groups and follow-up visits. For a laboratory workflow, they might represent experimental stages or decision points.

Recent findings suggest that the key is to make the relationships clear. What box comes first? Where does the pathway split? Which arrow connects to which endpoint? If the logic is ambiguous to a human reader, it will be ambiguous to the AI model, too.

Once the sketch is complete, I photograph it, upload the image to a vision-enabled language model and provide a detailed prompt. For instance:.

“Recreate the uploaded hand-drawn figure as a clean, editable academic flowchart in Draw.io-compatible XML format. Preserve the original structure as faithfully as possible, including box positions, arrows, dashed connectors, side boxes, branching pattern, and text content. This is a reconstruction task, not a redesign task. Use a plain white background, thin dark slate-grey borders, white box fills, thin connector lines, clean sans-serif text, and no shadows, gradients, or decorative elements. Make it publication-quality while keeping it recognizably the same diagram.”.

According to recent reports, the instruction “This is a reconstruction task, not a redesign task” is crucial. Scientific diagrams are not the place for creative completion. I want the model to reconstruct my structure, not improve it on my behalf.

Note also that this prompt indicates what the model should not change. I explicitly ask it to preserve wording, branching relationships and directionality. If the diagram contains notable numbers, doses or time points, I check each one manually.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03513-1.

Mauricio Pochettino's start to life as United manager could hardly have gone much worse, with the Argentinian finding his side two goals and one man down against arch-rivals Liverpool just 13 minutes into his tenure.

The one positive from the 4-0 defeat at Anfield is that surely the only way is up for Pochettino, and a positive result on the road in Europe would be a step in the right direction.

United's 3-2 comeback success over Roma three weeks ago, which proved to be Michael Carrick's last victory in charge, put them on six points at the halfway point of the league phase, so they will likely need one more win to finish in the top 24 and qualify for the knockout phase play-offs.

To do that, Pochettino has to sort out a defence that has conceded more goals (34) than any other in Europe's top five leagues this season. Left-back Luke Shaw is closing in on his return from injury, while captain Bruno Fernandes will face his former club for the first time since leaving Sporting in 2020.

Sporting CP 2-2 Manchester United.

United can't stop conceding goals at the moment, but they should be able to hurt Sporting — and that could save them here.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The report spans more than 150 pages, but its conclusion can be summed up in a single sentence: "The global situation regarding freedom of religion and belief deteriorated during the reporting period," said Thomas Rachel, the German government's commissioner for freedom of religion and belief, and a member of parliament for the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU). Recently adopted by the Cabinet, the government's fourth report on the subject covers developments from 2023 to 2025.

Recent findings suggest that the government has issued a dedicated report on freedom of religion and belief around the world. According to the report, this freedom is facing "increasing pressure" globally. The focus is not primarily on the suppression of religious institutions or structures, but on the situation of individuals who hold a religious belief, or none at all.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The importance of religious freedom is reflected in the way the government commissioner describes the concern: "Religion and faith are of great importance to four out of five people around the world and are central to their identity. People wake up with God and go to sleep with God. It is part of their everyday lives." Research by the Pew Research Center suggests that about 84% of the world's population identifies with a certain religion.

At a time when authoritarian regimes are gaining ground and expanding their surveillance capabilities, the report paints a bleak picture. The growing number of violent conflicts, the rise of authoritarian rule, and the spread of populism have led to "painful restrictions on freedom of religion and belief around the world.".

The German government report does not attempt to provide a statistical tally of attacks or the number of people facing persecution. Instead, it examines 30 countries as case studies where, in the federal government's view, freedom of religion and belief is being restricted. These include about six countries each from Africa, Asia, and the Arab world. In Europe, the report focuses on Belarus, Russia, Ukraine, and Turkey, while in Latin America it highlights Mexico, Nicaragua, and Cuba. It also identifies shortcomings in five of the world's six most populous countries: China, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, and Nigeria.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, regarding India, the report refers to "Hindu nationalist efforts" that threaten the equal treatment of all officially recognized religions. It states that the generally peaceful coexistence of different faiths is "repeatedly overshadowed by tensions and, at times, violence." Both Muslim and Christian communities report growing intolerance and hate speech. According to the report, violent Hindu extremist groups have carried out a "large number of physical attacks" against Muslims, while the police and government authorities often respond inadequately.

It has been revealed that in China, the German government identifies a "significant tightening of the legal framework of state control at the expense of freedom of religion and belief." According to the report, this particularly affects Uyghurs, Tibetans and churches that lack official state approval and are subject to harsh measures by the authorities. The law on the "Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress," which came into force on July 1, 2026, subordinates religion to "the formation of national identity" and patriotic education.

One of the countries where the situation has deteriorated most dramatically is Nicaragua, which has severely restricted freedom of religion and belief since 2018. The repression has primarily targeted the Catholic Church. According to the report, "intimidation, persecution, imprisonment, and expulsion" have forced around 130 priests and nuns to leave the country.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The reports reserves some of its sharpest criticism for Kirill, the patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church. Under his leadership, the church has strongly supported Russia's war against Ukraine and portrayed it as a "holy war." According to the report, "weapons are blessed, Russian soldiers are absolved of their sins, and donations are collected for the war." It is perhaps the clearest example in the report of how religion can be used to justify oppression and violence.

The report explicitly addresses the threat posed by "transnational repression" (TNR), which it describes as a "growing global problem" that also affects Germany. The term refers to the persecution or intimidation of individuals by their country of origin beyond its own borders.

Ultimately, it argues, this amounts to a "continuation of domestic repression." Such "cross-border repression" has become considerably easier through the growing availability of digital means of repression, including smear campaigns on social media and spyware.

According to recent reports, these forms of pressure range from physical attacks on individuals to digital assaults such as online intimidation and defamation. In some cases, repression is also carried out by threatening family members who remain in the country of origin. Russia and Iran, for example, are identified as the "main perpetrators of transnational repression" in Germany.

China is a particularly prominent example of religious and ideological tensions. Repression by Beijing in Germany primarily targets members of groups that the country's Communist Party classifies as "hostile to the system." These include Uyghurs, Tibetans, and members of the Falun Gong movement. According to the report, they are "also subject to surveillance and repressive measures in Germany," while relatives living in China are pressured.

Thomas Rachel hopes the newly published report will be "discussed in as many Bundestag committees as possible" and that members of parliament will "engage with the issue accordingly." Previous government reports on the subject have been debated in the Bundestag plenary at least once and, in some cases, twice.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that the concern's place within the German government has also changed during the current legislative term. Commissioner Thomas Rachel is now based at the Foreign Ministry, while both of his predecessors since 2018 were attached to the Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development. Today, Rachel says, the importance of religion is being "taken into account" in German foreign policy. He also points to his involvement in the Foreign Ministry's diplomatic training programs.

According to recent reports, in doing so, the government led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) reversed a structural decision made by the previous center-left coalition, which was led from 2021 to 2025 by Chancellor Olaf Scholz of the Social Democratic Party (SPD). The Scholz government had reduced the problem's prominence by assigning it to the "Religion and Foreign Policy" division. Religion and foreign policy have now regained a more prominent place within government.

One example is the current foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, who has already visited the Vatican more often than his two predecessors combined. In addition, alongside Rachel, the ministry has for some time maintained a dedicated unit headed by an ambassador that deals with, among other things, "fundamental challenges relating to religion and foreign policy.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Manchester United turned to its data gurus in a bid to categorically prove Alexander Isak had no chance of reaching the ball as part of its evidence to overturn Leny Yoro’s red card.
  • Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United’s trip to Anfield for a last-man foul on Isak, which referee Sam Barrott determined fit the criteria for Denial Of A Goalscoring Opportunity (DOGSO).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:49 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 07:52 EST, 26 November 2026.

Manchester United turned to its data gurus in a bid to categorically prove Alexander Isak had no chance of reaching the ball as part of its evidence to overturn Leny Yoro’s red card.

Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United’s trip to Anfield for a last-man foul on Isak, which referee Sam Barrott determined fit the criteria for Denial Of A Goalscoring Opportunity (DOGSO).

The young United centre-back was shown a straight red card after VAR doubled down on the day, insisting that no ‘clear and obvious error’ had been made.

United successfully appealed the decision through an independent panel and the lengths they went to for their evidence submission has now come to light.

Bosses at United included three high-definition video clips of the incident in question, which used multiple different angles as well as speeds in slow-motion and in real time for the panel to consider.

United also submitted video evidence of a DOGSO sending off earlier this season for Brighton’s Pascal Struijk against Sunderland, which was also overturned on appeal.

Leny Yoro was sent off for Man United against Liverpool but the red card was later rescinded.

United showed that Isak would not have reached the ball if he'd have stayed on his feet.

The most fascinating element of United’s detailed evidence pack came via its data department, led by ex-Formula One guru Michael Sansoni.

United outlined in a letter to the appeal panel that a technical analysis of the incident saw boffins at Carrington calculate the probability of Isak reaching the ball following his heavy touch prior to contact from Yoro.

The data allowed for the possibility that Isak maintained his speed and direction from the moment his legs first made contact with Yoro to assess whether he would have got to the ball before United goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

United’s analysis concluded that Isak would have been 1.8 metres shy of reaching the ball even if all optimal speed and directional factors had been achieved.

The appeals commission, however, told United that that data, however detailed, was not verifiable and so had to be treated with ‘caution’.

Considering all the elements of United’s submission, the panel unanimously agreed that it was not a red card offence and did not meet the threshold for DOGSO, immediately overturning the decision and withdrawing all punishment against Yoro.

It has been revealed that ‘We can accept referee can make a mistake. But we have VAR. What were they doing?’ a fuming Mauricio Pochettino remarked on Tuesday of the original Yoro decision.

Sources indicate that ‘We are going to repeat the game? Play similar tools the game XI v XI? We have an unbelievable car but we have to be at the level to drive. We accept the technology.’.

Joshua Kimmich has criticised Bayern Munich over their handling of teammate Jamal Musiala, describing the club’s public conduct towards the midfielder — who suffers from a neurological condition that causes seizures — as "not Bayern-like".

According to recent reports, the comments follow public criticism from senior figures at Bayern regarding Musiala’s performances and contract. The player experienced two seizures on the pitch during pre-season fixtures, prompting opposition from the international players' union, FIFPRO.

A key squad member has now spoken out, warning that the club risks damaging its traditional family values.

"What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated in public," Kimmich told reporters after Bayern's 2-1 Champions League loss at Lille on Wednesday. "It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it's not bigger than a person. That's an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like either.".

Kimmich also questioned whether Musiala's ongoing struggles were more closely linked to physical injuries over the past two years, including a badly fractured leg at last year's Club World Cup, rather than his medical condition.

"It's not the case that he has problems because he's unprofessional. He's there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself," Kimmich added.

Bayern met with Musiala's representatives on Tuesday to clarify the timeline of events, rejecting speculation that the midfielder concealed his health condition prior to signing his recent contract extension.

Both the club and Musiala's representatives accept that he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after extending his contract.

"This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared," Bayern said.

Musiala went public with his diagnosis in August after collapsing on the pitch during two pre-season matches, alarming fans and fellow professionals.

Bayern coach Vincent Kompany stated at the time that the episodes were triggered by a change in Musiala's medication. He was rested for the start of the campaign and has since missed games due to a muscle injury.

It has been revealed that musiala came off the bench in the 76th minute of Wednesday's defeat at Lille, capping a difficult week for Bayern. Ballon D'Or winner Harry Kane injured his ankle on Friday and faces months on the sidelines, while Bayern have lost the lead in the Bundesliga and fallen to 15th in the Champions League standings.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some things are certain in life; death, taxes and Watford sacking another head coach.

At 11:51am on Sunday morning, the news everyone expected had arrived and Alessio Dionisi was relieved of his duties as Watford head coach after five months in charge, following a dismal 4-0 away defeat to Sheffield United, which left the club just one place above the relegation zone.

It was the latest in a series of lifeless performances from a Watford side that have looked ill-equipped for Championship football from the moment the season started.

Now, at a time where Watford need Championship experience more than ever, owner Gino Pozzo has turned to former Romania boss Edward Iordanescu, a man that has had 13 jobs in 15 years, never managed more than 60 games at any team and most importantly, never played or coached in England or in one of Europe’s major leagues.

Given Watford’s reputation with head coaches, many would joke Iordanescu’s appointment sounds like a match made in heaven.

For Hornets fans, though, it’s an act of desperation from a club that has no plan, structure or hope.

In truth, Dionisi is the latest in a series of head coaches who have been let down by owner Pozzo, chairman Scott Duxbury and technical director Gianluca Nani, who seem incapable of building a squad or supporting a head coach.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Things could have been so different for the Italian, because at the start of the season, there was clearly something there. Watford were excellent in their opening day win over Southampton - playing with real flair and intensity in the first half - and followed that up with draws against Wrexham and West Ham. It was clear the players respected the Italian.

However, the warning signs were already there. In the summer, Dionisi and supporters were told that Watford would prioritise experienced players in the transfer market. None arrived.

Nestory Irankunda, Imran Louza and Giorgi Chakvetadze - three key players - were sold and not replaced, with Watford starting the season with just two centre-backs on the club’s books and two fit central midfielders.

It has been revealed that the Italian sounded increasingly exasperated as his calls for reinforcements fell on deaf ears until the final few days of the window, where Watford eventually panicked and brought in Stephy Mavididi, Soumaila Coulibaly and Branimir Mlacic on loan. Myron Boadu and Michail Antonio arrived on free transfers.

Most of those players arrived unfit and come September, Dionisi was struggling to fill the bench as injuries took hold. The Italian never really recovered from embarrassing defeats to Burnley and Cardiff City, deploying a back five in recent weeks as he attempted to make the Golden Boys harder to beat.

In a recent development, quite frankly, Watford are unmanageable. Not even Pep Guardiola would be successful at Vicarage Road, because no head coach is given the opportunity to implement a style of play when they have to contend with poor recruitment, a leadership vacuum and a dressing room with seemingly poor attitudes.

Industry observers note that rob Edwards was promised he'd be backed in the transfer market come hell or high water by chairman Duxbury in the summer of 2022. Most of the signings he received didn't fit his system and he was sacked within two months of the season starting.

Recent findings suggest that after Edwards, Slaven Bilic thought he'd be able to sign players he wanted in the January transfer window. He received Joao Ferreira and Henrique Araujo - both of whom never looked suited to Championship football – as well as Ryan Porteous, Wesley Hoedt and Britt Assombalonga. Bilic was gone by March.

Sources indicate that then came Chris Wilder, who repeatedly called out the poor attitude within the dressing room and wasn't given a contract extension when his deal expired in the summer of 2023. After the wheels came off under Valerian Ismael, Tom Cleverley was promoted to head coach in 2024 and despite a thin squad, united the players and fans, having been a popular player at Vicarage Road during his playing days.

Once again, though, January arrived and Cleverley didn't get the options he so dearly needed, meaning Watford's form dropped off and he was sacked, somewhat harshly, at the end of the season.

Just last season, the popular Javi Gracia returned for a second spell in charge and had Watford in the play-off spots by January. He was promised additions, but none were forthcoming and ultimately the Spaniard decided the job wasn't worth his time. Gracia resigned, returning to Spain to spend time with his family.

In a recent development, in short, it's time the Watford ownership took a long, hard look at themselves, rather than the head coach. Has Iordanescu been appointed because no one sensible will take it? Any head coach worth his salt in England - and possibly now Italy, too - knows what they’re walking into.

In a recent interview with Roy Moore from the 1881 Movement, Pozzo tried shifting accountability for the club’s downfall, which can be traced back to the FA Cup Final in 2019. Since then, numerous decisions have, in the eyes of supporters, led to the erosion of the club's identity - fans have had enough.

Empty statements, the constant churn of players and head coaches, and what appears to be a lack of any real structure or plan - supporters are fed up.

The fact Watford closed their Under-21 setup, downgraded their academy and sold off the women's team this summer was a huge source of disappointment for fans, too, given the club’s rich history of bringing players through their youth system.

Unless there is a sudden change of approach overnight, Watford are only heading one way and that's down to League 1.

How to become a football referee

📅 01 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1302 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that honestly, for me it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done.
  • Louise Thompson, women's referee pathway officer for the Irish Football Association, international FIFA referee, and PremierLeague referee in Northern Ireland.
  • Looking after female referees within Northern Ireland, trying to recruit, retain and give them experience within their games to pushthrough into top level refereeing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that honestly, for me it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done. You find so much more out about yourself that you probably never knew.

Who are you and what is your job role?

Louise Thompson, women's referee pathway officer for the Irish Football Association, international FIFA referee, and PremierLeague referee in Northern Ireland.

What does a women's referee pathway officer do?

Looking after female referees within Northern Ireland, trying to recruit, retain and give them experience within their games to pushthrough into top level refereeing.

What kind of training do you give to aspiring referees?

So from going through recruitment courses first of all, and then we do the beginners course with referees, just giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge, then we will also do a practical part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we'll go through scenarios, positioning, things around free kick management for example, other set pieces likecorners, penalty setup, what you do as a referee day to day, even pre match stuff as well, so when you arrive at the grounds, how you check the pitch, check all the equipment is there, how you would interact with players, coaches and then just again, maybe createlike a role play sort of environment so that they know that they're not going totally blind into that sort of situation.

Have you always been passionate about football?

Football was a passion of mine, even when I was younger, primary school age, we just didn't have very many female teams, so it normally meant playing with the boys and the boys teams and stuff up until I was about 14, which was the minimum age here you can join senior ladies football team, which is what I did, and played there for 14 years at a club here locally, including up until the Women's Premiership, so it was great to be involved in football, but I always loved watching football, playing football, anything to do with football, I was always there and interested.

How did you go from playing football to being a referee?

According to recent reports, becoming a referee for me sort of happened by chance to be honest. It was during a game, one time I got an injury, quite a bad injury to my knee and then I had seen luckily that the referee course was being advertised. So I signed up for it, but I also signed up for a coaching course pretty much at the same time, maybe about six weeks apart. I wasnât really sure which role I wanted to follow, but over that winter I had been pushed into refereeing a wee bit and said sure, why not, Iâll give it a go, it'd be a bit of extra fitness before my season restarts, and then just fell in love with it from there and never looked back.

What subjects did you study at school and university?

Coming through school I always picked PE, so I did my GCSE PE and then I also did A-level PE and then when I went onto university,I had the sport and exercise science as well within that, so I think it gives you a good understanding of obviously how your body works, and your proposal and training, stuff like that as well so you know when you're working nutrition wise, things that you need to know,especially as you reach the top level, just to make sure that you're getting the most out of your body.

What are your top tips for becoming a referee?

In a recent development, I would say definitely give it a try for sure. You never know until you do it. I think even when I was a player, I probably never imaginedthat I would be a referee and that I would even achieve and have experienced what Iâve been able to experience. So you never knowuntil you give it a go, but it's also about probably pushing yourself out of your comfort zone, being comfortable with being uncomfortable in situations like that. It's maybe not always as bad as it probably seems it's going to be. There's probably a lot more stigma around being a referee - who wants to be a referee? - but honestly for me, it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done.

It has been revealed that with a lifelong love of football, Louise Thompson followed her passion for the game, first as a player and now as a referee. As well as refereeing Fifa and NIFL Premiership matches, she also works for the Irish Football Association as the women's referee pathway officer, recruiting and developing up-and-coming female refs.

Louise Thompson on refereeing the Women's Irish Cup final.

If you're interested in becoming a referee, it's something you can get involved with from a young age through local referee courses. The minimum age to become a qualified referee varies depending on where in the UK you live:.

According to recent reports, in her role as a women's referee pathway officer, Louise oversees latest referees right from the initial recruitment courses stage: "We then do the beginners' course with referees, giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge," she says. "We also do a hands-on part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we go through different scenariosâ¦ exactly what you do as a referee, and day-to-day practical stuff as wellâ¦ The idea is to give them all the basics and fundamentals before they go into a game so that they're prepared.".

All four UK nations have established pathways for referee development and progression. Starting out at grassroots level, it's possible to progress all the way to Fifa!

Recent findings suggest that louise's first games were youth games: "I still remember my first game to this day," she says. "It was an under-13 game, and I was definitely the most nervous person on the pitch." She explains: "Over time, you'll get mentors who will come and watch you, give you advice, give you feedback" which will help you to progress to higher levels of the game.

As well as PE, Louise has found that languages are really helpful in this line of work, "especially when you're dealing with a lot of international games and people coming along," she says. "If you can learn some languages, it's very, very useful.".

You could get into this role by training with a professional body.

Sources: National Careers Service, GOV.UK, FA, IFA, SFA, and FAW.

Enzo Maresca had two home games in four days to get Manchester City into decent shape for Sunday’s clash against Arsenal, which now feels like a must-win. On Tuesday, however, they ended up being taunted by Rasmus Hojlund on another evening that raised more questions than answers.

It has been revealed that it is now one win in seven for Maresca, who cannot keep a clean sheet and has a £327m midfield that have played well individually, but is yet to form a unit. Worryingly, their reliable source of goals, Erling Haaland, had his quietest game of the season. It required Rayan Cherki to rescue a point against Napoli.

It has been revealed that maresca needs to find a solution in the next five days before heading to the Emirates to face the champions in what could be a defining weekend for the season. Defeat would put them nine points off the pace, with Maresca still trying to find his best combination of players to pick.

Club captain Rúben Dias was on the bench here and Josko Gvardiol was left out of the draw against Fulham at the weekend, which also ended as a draw rather than a morale-boosting win to get City out of their slump.

Industry observers note that there is enough quality in City’s midfield to trouble Arsenal, but the conundrum for Maresca is how to fit them all into his system. Elliot Anderson was pushed towards the right against Napoli rather than in a central position to control the game, while Ayyoub Bouaddi was often alongside “inverted” full-back Nico O’Reilly.

In a recent development, bouaddi indicated his attacking instincts with City’s first equaliser; incredibly his first goal as a professional. There cannot be many £86m players who have yet to score in senior football. Enzo Fernandez also started against Napoli but was quiet before being taken off for the last half an hour.

“We have so much quality, so it’s about getting the quality out in every player. We have to regroup, stay positive and bring energy on the pitch and try to do our best.

According to recent reports, “We go to the champions, so it’s the most difficult game of the season going to the champions away. We need a top performance from every single player.”.

A penny for the thoughts of Khaldoon Al Mubarak and Aleksander Ceferin, who sat next to each other in the Etihad directors’ box.

Jérémy Doku had been brought on as a sub seconds before Napoli scored, then played his part in Bouaddi’s equaliser. From a short corner, Doku pulled the ball back for his team-mate to finish with a first-time side-foot shot.

Kevin De Bruyne has been lined up for a January move to PSV Eindhoven, with the Dutch club working on a deal to land one of the Premier League’s greatest players when the window opens.

De Bruyne, 35, has been at Napoli since the start of last season but it is understood that a move away from the Serie A club is now on the horizon. He is still under contract at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona so PSV will pay a fee to land him as they look to retain their Eredivisie title.

At Manchester City, De Bruyne won six Premier League titles and was part of their Treble-winning team that won the Champions League. During the last 18 months at Napoli he has suffered injury issues, had a row with team-mate on the pitch and was quoted as saying he was glad Antonio Conte left as head coach.

“Not a lot I can say for the moment,” noted De Bruyne when asked about his future. “I have played at 100% until now and obviously I am not 20 years old, I am turning 36.

“There is a lot of things going in my mind but there is not a lot to say. I am playing good football, trying to help the team to do well and it has been a bit of a challenging season with a lot of things happening.”.

It is matchday five of the Champions League as Manchester City host Napoli at the Etihad. These sides last met back in September 2025, with Manchester City winning 2-0 at home courtesy of goals from Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku. Manchester City’s cause was helped by an early red card for Napoli’s Giovanni Di Lorenzo. Napoli’s only win over Manchester City came all the way back in November 2011 when they won 2-1 after a double from Edinson Cavani.

Recent findings suggest that manchester City have won three of their opening four Champions League matches this season, with their only defeat coming at home against back-to-back champions PSG. They drew 1-1 at home against Fulham in the league on Saturday, which means they are now without a league win in four games.

According to recent reports, “We are always looking to win games, no matter the competition,” Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca said. “For sure, the four games in a row in the Premier League that we did not win has been a shame. Tomorrow [tonight] we have a chance to win the game and continue our path in the Champions League that at the moment has been very good. First of all, it is crucial to qualify and then probably, if you are not able to finish in the top eight, you have two more games that with the amount of games that we have, it is always important to reduce games. So the target is to try and finish in the top eight.”.

It has been revealed that napoli, managed by Massimiliano Allegri, have struggled thus far in this season’s Champions League, winning just one of their opening four games and are all the way down in 27th. They come into tonight’s match off the back of a 1-0 home win over Torino in Serie A on the weekend courtesy of former Manchester United midfielder Scott McTominay’s winning goal. However, they still sit down in eighth in the Italian top flight, a massive 14 points off the top through just 12 games.

Recent findings suggest that “This match will not be decisive,” Allegri mentioned. “It is a simple mathematical equation, but obviously we will try to do well, even against a great team like Manchester City. It will be a beautiful and fascinating challenge and we want to play to the best of our ability. Ultimately, our goal is to qualify. We must not repeat the mistakes we made in Porto, where we played a great game for 70 minutes and then let ourselves go, conceding chances too easily. We will have to be able to play both with and without possession.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

WSL Football, the organisation responsible for operating the top two tiers of women’s football in the UK, has reached an agreement in principle for its clubs not to make sponsorship deals with betting companies.

In a recent development, instead, the organisation has agreed to pursue sponsorship deals with brands from different industries, reports The Athletic. The outlet states that six additional sponsorship opportunities were made available ahead of the 2024/25 season, and these were filled by Apple, Airbnb, British Gas, Mercedes, Tesco and WTW.

While the agreement applies to WSL Football’s own commercial partnerships, it does not stop individual WSL or WSL2 clubs from signing sponsorship deals with gambling companies.

Rather, it sets a different direction for WSL Football’s league-level partnerships, giving the leagues the chance to shape their own commercial future. The organisation wants to continue aiding the growth of the women’s domestic game, while combating issues such as player welfare, gambling-related online abuse and fluctuating attendances.

In a recent development, the changes also come at a time when English football is starting to take a wider look at gambling and related sponsorships. At the start of this season, the Premier League’s voluntary ban on betting sponsors appearing on the front of match-day shirts came into effect, while the Premier League, EFL, FA and WSL also introduced a Code of Conduct for gambling-related sponsorship agreements in 2024.

Nevertheless, betting companies still feature prominently among sponsors at clubs throughout the top divisions in the men’s game, with Betway signing a deal with Manchester United and clubs such as Leeds and Nottingham Forest also agreeing upcoming deals over the summer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Working on one of the world's biggest football video games is the perfect combination of my two biggest passions, gaming and football.

Industry observers note that I'm CJ Ramson. I work on the creation of football video games. I work on Football Manager as an associate QA manager. QA stands for quality assurance.

Sources indicate that we're the ones that test the game. We make sure everything works, and we work closely with the developers to try and make the most realistic simulation of football.

It has been revealed that growing up, I loved football, whether that was playing football or playing football video games with my friends. I'd always be doing one or the other. With the video games, the thing that really drew me to them was I've always been into the tactical side of the game, either being able to control the players or create your own tactics.

So a typical day for us, we'll get a upcoming build in from the developers. We'll test it as a QA team, and we'll look for either bugsor ways that we can improve the game. That can be anything from the runs that players make, to decisions they make on the ball, what the team instructions and tactics do. So there's a lot of areas for us to cover. Our final goal is to make it as realistic to real football as possible.

So even though my background was in coaching, there was a lot of transferable skills that I learned and developed through my time coaching that I managed to transfer into this. So whether that's being really analytical and having a good eye for detail and knowingwhen to pick things out and what to look for, or it could be things like timekeeping and making sure things run perfectly on time, and working with other people as well. So social skills where you have to work within a team or even lead a team.

The animation he makes, and the ball physics as well, where the ball goes off after the save.".

So as much as I loved playing football, I realised quite early on I probably wasn't going to be a professionalfootballer. But I wanted to work in football and find. So at college, I studied sports science, and that's where I found my love of coaching. I did my FA Level 1 and then went on to do my FA Level 2. After I left college, I got a job at Arsenal, which was unpaid, working with them, learning how to develop my coaching skills. Which then led to me having a full-time paid job at Fulham Football Club, working with the youth teams, working with the academy teams. And then that eventually led to me going to an event. I saw an opportunity where you could apply for a job in Football Manager. It was something that naturally I was interested in, had a conversation with them, and realised it was definitely something that I would love to do.

So I went to the networking event at Kick It Out, and that was an opportunity for me to network with other football coaches, other people within the gaming industries, and have a really good insight to different jobs in football gaming. Without doing that, I wouldn't have the opportunity to meet the people at Football Manager and see a newly introduced job in gaming, which I wouldn't have beenaware of.

Sources indicate that one of the highlights of my career so far is working on the in-and-out-of-possession system on FM 26. This is something we see in real football all the time, so being part of the team that brought that to life and brought it into the game was super cool.

Working within the football industry is a dream come true. Being able to work on something that I'm passionate about, that is played and enjoyed by millions of people, is an amazing feeling for me and an amazing opportunity that I have. And yeah, I love it.

Ever wondered who makes sure your video games are great? This guy!

CJ works as an associate quality assurance manager on the video game Football Manager. His team test the game to make sure everything works, and collaborate with the developers to create the most realistic simulation of football.

There are lots of different ways to progress in the gaming industry.

CJ works in the QA (Quality Assurance) team, testing games. In this team, his career progression has followed this path:.

QA tester --> QA lead --> QA manager.

His team is just one of the options, though. "There are lots of other roles within the industry too, including production, game design, social media and development, where developers help to code the game," he explains. "Depending on your skills and interests, there are different pathways you can take that you might enjoy and be suited to.".

Sources indicate that there are different roles in video game testing. CJ notes that: "Salaries can vary depending on your role and the manufacturer you work for. They can range from around Â£20,000 to Â£50,000 and upwards." The higher salaries in this range could apply when you've gained more experienced and progressed in your career.

CJ is now a quality assurance manager, but he started out as a quality assurance tester. Find out more about the role of QA tester below. This role can have various other job titles, such as games tester, computer games tester, and video games tester.

You could get into this role via a university course, a college course (such as a Level 3 Diploma in Creative Media, an A-level in Computing, or a T-level in Digital Software Development (England only)), an apprenticeship, or applying directly if you have relevant experience.

In a recent development, this information is a guide and is constantly changing. Please check the National Careers Service website for the latest information and all the qualifications needed and the GOV.UK website for more on T-levels.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Russian  ballistic missile strikes on Ukraine's southern city of Kryvyi Rih — President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown — killed two people and wounded dozens of others, local officials said Saturday.

The attacks come amid little progress in talks to end the nearly five-year-old war and after Ukraine, on three occasions this week, struck the Kerch bridge linking Russian-occupied Crimea with Russia.

Russian President Vladimir Putin had vowed a "painful" response to the Kerch attack, as the bridge is vital for war supplies for Russian forces in the south.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Among the dead in Friday evening's double-tap strikes on Kryvyi Rih were a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, while several children were among the 60 wounded, the Ukrainian officials said.

Several fires broke out and damage was caused to about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial facility, Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of the city administration, wrote on Telegram.

Moscow, meanwhile, confirmed a further strike on Friday night in Kryvyi Rih.

Russia's Defense Ministry said a thermal power plant in the city was hit, along with a power substation in the region of Rivne, on the opposite side of the country.

Both facilities supply electricity to the industry supporting Ukraine's military, the ministry added.

Elsewhere in the nearly five-year-long war, Russia ​also struck a ​cargo vessel ‌near Odesa, which Moscow remarked was carrying dual-use goods ​for ⁠the Ukrainian military.

Eleven people, including two children, were wounded when a Russian drone attacked a five-story apartment building in the northeastern Kharkiv region, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Saturday.

One person was wounded in a Russian attack on the capital, Kyiv, according to the service.

In Russia, local officials said Saturday that Ukrainian drone attacks wounded three people in the Bryansk and Belgorod border regions.

Finland, meanwhile, said it detected a drone attack on Saturday morning on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea, prompting Prime Minister Petteri Orpo to warn that the war is "spilling over into our immediate vicinity.".

After damage to Russia's Kerch bridge to Crimea, Zelenskyy warned in an interview with US broadcaster NBC that the structure "will not remain standing anyway.".

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yeremy Pino is the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow-card suspension.
  • Crystal Palace's Yeremy Pino has become the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow card suspension after accumulating five bookings since the 2026-27 season began.
  • Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash were the first players to receive a ban for collecting five yellow cards before gameweek 19.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yeremy Pino is the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow-card suspension.

Crystal Palace's Yeremy Pino has become the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow card suspension after accumulating five bookings since the 2026-27 season began.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash were the first players to receive a ban for collecting five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 17 players sitting on four bookings after 11 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

In a recent development, after that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

Sources indicate that for players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

The following players have received a one-match ban and will now receive a two-match ban if they reach ten bookings before game week 32:.

Yeremy Pino - Crystal Palace (five yellow cards).

Matt Crooks - Hull City (five yellow cards).

Matty Cash - Aston Villa (five).

If any of the following players receive another Premier League yellow card before the season's halfway point, they will be banned for one match:.

Vitaly Janelt - Brentford (four).

Oli McBurnie - Hull City (four).

Harry Maguire - Manchester United (four).

Pascal Gross - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Ethan Ampadu - Leeds United (four).

Oliver Boscagli - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Adam Smith - Bournemouth (four).

Marcus Tavernier - Bournemouth (four).

Antonio Silva - Bournemouth (four).

Alexis Mac Allister - Liverpool (four).

James McAtee - Nottingham Forest (four).

Chema Andres - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Bradley Barcola - Liverpool (four).

Murillo - Nottingham Forest (four).

The following players will miss their club's next set of fixtures:.

Yeremy Pino - Crytsal Palce (yellow card suspension).

Jean-Philippe Mateta - Crystal Palace (red card suspension).

Igor Thiago - Brentford (red card suspension).

Costinha - Brighton & Hove Albion (red card suspension).

Leny Yoro - Manchester United (red card suspension).

James Tarkowski - Everton (red card suspension).

Published: 05:50 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 08:38 EST, 26 November 2026.

Former Man United midfielder Darron Gibson has revealed the harrowing extent of his sleeping pill addiction and broke down in tears as his wife recalled the moment she thought he had died.

Gibson, who played for United 31 times between 2005-2012, secretly battled against anxiety during his career and turned to sleeping pills to help switch his mind off.

He began taking the pills after suffering a knee injury for the Republic of Ireland in 2013 and developed an addiction that led to him consuming 14 every night and on one occasion led to wife Danielle thinking he'd died.

Recent findings suggest that opening up on RTE’s Howler podcast, Danielle remembered her husband suffering a seizure in 2021, saying: 'When the ambulance staff came in, he had blue lips, I thought he had gone. I was being treated for shock. I just thought: "At least he’s not struggling anymore." Next minute (sharp intake of breath), he's back.'.

Gibson replied: 'Ultimately, if that hadn’t have happened, I wouldn’t be here now.'.

Danielle then said: 'I think you’d be dead', prompting Gibson to break down in tears, admitting 'probably'.

Darron Gibson (left) spoke about suffering from sleeping pill addiction and his wife Danielle (right) opened up about thinking he'd died in 2021 after a seizure.

Gibson broke down in tears at the painful memory but is now far happier and in recovery.

Gibson was convicted of drink driving in 2015 during his downward spiral and was playing for Everton at the time.

It has been revealed that he added: 'Looking back, who takes five sleeping tablets at 10 in the morning and doesn’t go to sleep? It’s ridiculous. But it’s where I was. It’s what I was doing.

'I think Everton thought they were looking after me by not punishing me, which I really appreciated at the time.

Sources indicate that 'And I don’t blame them for any of this, but I think if they’d punished me, maybe I would have changed. But I didn’t and kept going.'.

Three years later at Sunderland, he consumed a mix of pills and vodka before crashing into parked cars. He was spared prison time but had a 40-month driving ban and the Black Cats ripped up his contract.

He recalled: 'Took a few sleeping tablets, thought I was going to go to sleep. Next thing I know, I’m in handcuffs in the back of a police van.'.

Danielle, who worked as a specialist in addiction services while Gibson was at Sunderland, notes Gibson was one of many with similar challenges in the professional game.

In a recent development, she went on: 'I understand that football is a business. I just think they should have had a duty of care.

Gibson and Danielle are seen together at the Premier of Wayne Rooney's documentary in 2022.

Gibson poses with the Premier League trophy after Man United won the title in 2011.

'He’s not the only one that was struggling, there were so many lads, whether it be sleeping tablets or mental health or depression or anxiety or booze.

'There were so many that were almost denied access to services that I feel should have been available to all of them.'.

Gibson is now in recovery and indicates he is in a far happier state of mind than in his playing days. He ended his career at Salford City five years ago following a brief spell at Wigan.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • The Independent Football Regulator could force Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi ownership out of English football if the guilty verdicts over breaches of Premier League financial rules are upheld.
  • Sources indicate that city were found guilty of nearly every charge brought against them by the league when the commission’s verdict was published in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

The Independent Football Regulator could force Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi ownership out of English football if the guilty verdicts over breaches of Premier League financial rules are upheld.

Sources indicate that city were found guilty of nearly every charge brought against them by the league when the commission’s verdict was published in September. A three-person adjudication panel found that the club had systematically inflated revenues and disguised losses by a combined £900m through “sham” deals between 2009 and 2018, aiding their rapid ascent to the summit of the game.

In a recent development, the club have always strongly denied wrongdoing and have appealed against the commission’s verdict. If City’s appeal fails, a sanction hearing will follow and is expected to recommend seismic sporting and financial punishments.

Separately, the regulator (IFR), which was established last year following the fallout from the European Super League scandal, has legal powers to investigate and sanction both the club and any individuals involved in breaching rules.

It has been revealed that the IFR grants operating licenses to football clubs and has the power to withdraw them. It also carries powers to order officials who it deems unsuitable to “take all reasonable steps to cease to be an owner of the club” within a given time frame.

The regulator faces a major test of its ability to referee the English game, given both the enormity of the City case and Abu Dhabi’s political and economic relationship with the UK.

Some senior figures within English football were concerned by comments from prime minister Andy Burnham appearing to downplay the significance of the verdict when it first emerged, although Downing Street later clarified that Burnham’s view is that no-one is “above the rules”.

But David Kogan, the IFR chair, has told parliament’s Digital, Culture, Media and Sport select committee that the regulator is prepared to take strong action against City, if necessary.

“Forget the name of the club, forget the size of the club, forget the scale of the glitch,” Kogan stated. “We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size.

“We absolutely will have to take the appropriate action as laid out in the legislation, depending on the circumstances as they come to us, which are the evidence that’s been presented and collated by the independent commission of the Premier League and by any judgement that takes place on that evidence through an appeal.

“But in one sense, the evidence has already been judged by those cases having been found guilty, so we will absolutely have the stomach to do so.”.

City are owned by City Football Group, a parent company controlled by Emirati royal Sheikh Mansour via his Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) investment vehicle. The commission found that ADUG money was used to artificially inflate City’s revenues, something the club continues to dispute.

Sources indicate that kogan added: “Would I, with an organisation that has a relatively latest, fairly young staff, that’s been going for less than a year, would I have chosen to have this particular issue in our laps this early? Well, probably not. But the truth is, if we don’t act – assuming those circumstances are triggered – if we don’t act, what is the purpose of having a football regulator?

“So I think we have to absolutely, clearly be seen to be doing the job that you as legislators have asked us to do, and we absolutely will do that, whatever that means.”.

City’s appeal against the commission’s verdict has no set timetable but is expected to be concluded early in the new year, with the sanctions hearing then set to follow if any or all of the verdicts are upheld.

City’s most recent statement, on 2 October, read: “Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the Club lodged its comprehensive Appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter.

Industry observers note that “The Club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe. The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

“We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete.”.

Wirtz follows rich Liverpool heritage with star showing in win over Brugge

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it had to be this way.
  • The late Kevin Keegan thrashed home a free-kick at this stadium 50 years ago to win Liverpool the Uefa Cup and Sir Kenny Dalglish was the hero at Wembley in 1978 when his deft finish ensured the European Cup was retained.
  • That jersey means those who have subsequently worn it have had high standards to keep.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it had to be this way. Liverpool No 7s have historically defined matches against Club Brugge, so it was entirely appropriate that Florian Wirtz preserved that rich heritage.

The late Kevin Keegan thrashed home a free-kick at this stadium 50 years ago to win Liverpool the Uefa Cup and Sir Kenny Dalglish was the hero at Wembley in 1978 when his deft finish ensured the European Cup was retained.

That jersey means those who have subsequently worn it have had high standards to keep. Although this fixture did not carry the heft of past occasions, it was symbolic that Wirtz, the incumbent, decorated this contest and propelled Liverpool a step closer to the knockout phase.

Industry observers note that on another night Alexander Isak would have expected his two goals to take the headlines, but he would have appreciated more than anyone the magic spells that Wirtz kept casting. The Swede had a glorious view of the strike that essentially secured three points in Belgium’s frozen north.

The idea of Brugge playing in the biggest club fixture of all, sadly, seems fanciful now given how much the footballing landscape has changed. But they are a progressive side, full of attacking wit, and they had ambitions and, on another evening, would have done some damage.

Sources indicate that how often, though, do you see sides these days undo their good work by being overambitious when playing out from the back? Yann Sommer has had a distinguished career, the Swiss goalkeeper has played for Bayern Munich and Inter Milan, but he is 37 and his aberration was decisive.

Industry observers note that he put Kyriani Sabbe in all manner of trouble with a loose pass, Bradley Barcola picked the right-back’s pocket and nudged it on swiftly to Dominik Szoboszlai, who in turn fed Isak. With the goal at his mercy from six yards, the striker was never going to miss.

Alexander Isak finds the back of the net to give Liverpool the lead against Club Brugge! 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/vZbiHKkpiy.

It has been revealed that “He is in a great moment,” Andoni Iraola, Liverpool’s head coach, stated of his striker. “When the team is playing well and getting good results everyone looks better. In the second half we defended lower and knew there would be space to exploit. In one of those moments, he killed the game.”.

In a recent development, liverpool are not perfect, by any means, but the closer you watch them, the more obvious it is that they are grasping what Iraola wants. They will be a good team when it does click, but these are just the first steps of the journey. The first half proved it.

Some moves broke down with a misplaced pass and Brugge were often let off the hook when they were guilty of over-elaboration. Iraola wants Liverpool to be ruthless, but his mood soured for a period, not least when Victor Muñoz injured his knee in an incident when he was trying to win back possession.

“A knock on the knee and we have to test it,” Iraola noted. “That was the worst part of the night. It is very early to tell but it was very painful at that moment. He was better after the game.”.

So, too, was Iraola, who was especially pleased that Liverpool recorded their first Champions League clean sheet of the season and, in the process, stopped Brugge – who had scored in 19 consecutive games – from finding a way through.

Sources indicate that there were several reasons this was the case: Jérémy Jacquet, for instance, never put a foot wrong – what a smart signing he has proved to be. He more than did his bit to retain order in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, who was given the chance to catch his breath before the Merseyside derby.

It was tough for Liverpool in the second period, as Brugge attacked the end of the stadium where their noisy ultras created a cacophony. Yet they handled the situation well, even if Iraola looked ready to combust at one stage, receiving a yellow card for protesting too much to the officials.

“I saw the referee beforehand, I know him from Spain and I knew this was coming,” Iraola said.

Liverpool, of course, won both and a feature has just been shown on Belgian TV from Bruges’s perspective of the defeat at Wembley. It has been revealed that liverpool have travelled over to Belgium to take on Club Brugge on matchday five in the Champions League. These sides have met competitively three times before and they have all come in finals, resulting in famous nights for Liverpool. In 1976, Liverpool beat Club Brugge 4-3 on aggregate across two legs to win the Uefa Cup. Then, Kenny Dalglish scored the only goal of the game at Wembley back in May 1978 as Liverpool won the European Cup for the second straight season, becoming the first English side to do so.

Liverpool, who have won 13 of their previous 17 matches against Belgian sides, won their first three Champions League games, beating Atletico Madrid, LASK and Villarreal but lost 3-2 away at Fenerbahce on matchday four despite leading twice in that game. After tonight’s game in Belgium, Liverpool’s remaining games in the Champions League are against Porto, Inter Milan and Lens. Andoni Iraola’s side come into this game with a spring in their step after thrashing rivals Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield on Sunday.

“A win [against Manchester United on Sunday] is always great but you do not have time to celebrate with this schedule,” Iraola remarked. “By Monday, we were already watching analysis of Club Brugge. I have enjoyed analysing them [Brugge], they are very energetic and have had an incredible run of games. I think we will have to be at a very good level, otherwise it is going to be very difficult. They have players who can make the difference and obviously we do as well, so I expect quite an open game. We are both aggressive, both want to press, there will be spaces and hopefully we can win the one-vs-one battles.”.

Industry observers note that club Brugge have made a strong start to this season’s Champions League; after losing their first game to Aston Villa, they have since won their next three, including wins over Inter Milan, Lens and PSV. That puts them on the same number of points as Liverpool and are just one place behind. In the Belgian Pro League at the weekend, they thrashed Mechelen 5-1 and they sit second in the Belgian top flight, one point behind Union SG.

Industry observers note that “I am proud of the players and what they have achieved against Aston Villa, Inter, Lens and PSV,” Club Brugge boss Ivan Leko remarked. “We know we should be grateful to be here, but we really want to try to show that Belgian football is fun to watch and we can win matches. I am proud, but I know we are a substantial club. You are only as good as your last match. We know what happened in the past, so there is also a nice connection between both clubs and the supporters. It is a special fixture to play, but we are not here just to enjoy the Champions League; we want to win and that is what we are going to try to do tomorrow [tonight].”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England are a seeded side for the Nations League quarter-finals after topping their group.

The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however Northern Ireland's draw against Hungary saw them top Group B2 and secure promotion to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

The Republic of Ireland finished second in Group B3 and so will take part in a League A/B promotion play-off in March.

The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

England have sealed their place in the last eight as Group A3 winners and could face:.

They cannot face A3 runners-up Spain as teams must be drawn against sides from other groups.

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the international break between 25-30 March.

Seeded teams get to play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

Nations that reach the semi-finals can bid those penultimate matches as well as the final.

The remaining dates for the Nations League are:.

Quarter-finals first leg: 25-27 March.

Quarter-finals second leg: 28-30 March.

Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June.

Latest Update: Why Man City can't wear their newly introduced kit in Premier League

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (387 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City will only be wearing their orange kit for selected Champions League games.
  • Manchester City sported a upcoming orange fourth kit during their Champions League draw with Napoli on Tuesday - but will not be able to wear it in the Premier League.
  • Top-flight clubs in England can only wear a maximum of three strips in a league campaign, meaning Enzo Maresca's side cannot play in their newly introduced kit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City will only be wearing their orange kit for selected Champions League games.

Manchester City sported a upcoming orange fourth kit during their Champions League draw with Napoli on Tuesday - but will not be able to wear it in the Premier League.

Top-flight clubs in England can only wear a maximum of three strips in a league campaign, meaning Enzo Maresca's side cannot play in their newly introduced kit.

However, there is no limit in the Champions League, meaning City can wear their new strip for the rest of their European campaign.

City can also wear the kit in the FA Cup, provided that an application is made to the Football Association, as well as a reason for its requested use.

That is why Arsenal were allowed to play in a white fourth strip in the 2025-26 FA Cup as part of their campaign to combat youth knife crime in London.

Fans could scan the badge on City's 2025-26 fourth kit to receive items in a video game.

City also released a green fourth kit in 2025-26 with a gaming-inspired theme.

The kit, debuted during their Champions League victory over Villarreal, featured an NFC chip in the club badge that fans could scan to unlock gaming rewards.

The club released another fourth kit in the 2024-25 season co-designed by Noel Gallagher in tribute to the 30th anniversary of Oasis' 1994 album 'Definitely Maybe'.

It was worn in the Champions League by the men's team against Inter Milan and Paris St-Germain, and the women's team against Paris FC and Barcelona.

A fifth kit was also used by the men's team during the 2025 Club World Cup.

During the 2023-24 season, the women's side also sported a Chinese New Year-inspired shirt in a League Cup victory against rivals Manchester United.

While the Premier League is more restrictive over the number of kits that can be released - the rules are more relaxed in other European leagues.

Napoli wore 13 strips during the 2021-22 season; including a Halloween kit, four different Diego Maradona tributes and four Europa League-specific kits.

It has been revealed that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Joshua Zirkzee insisted Manchester United must focus on their own performance rather than pointing fingers at controversial refereeing following their 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday night.

The tie in Lisbon was marked by a series of contentious calls from Polish match official Szymon Marciniak, prompting former United captain and BBC Radio 5 Live pundit Ashley Young to describe the officiating as "a disgrace".

Marciniak disallowed Amad Diallo’s first-half equaliser by blowing his whistle before the ball hit the back of an empty net, having wrongly judged Youri Tielemans to have fouled Goncalo Inacio in the buildup.

The United midfielder’s frustration over the booking was compounded when he received a second yellow card in the closing stages of the match.

The referee also ruled out a late winner for United after being directed to the pitchside monitor, deciding goalkeeper Kaique Pereira had been fouled by Patrick Dorgu.

However, speaking in a post-match interview with MUTV, Zirkzee said: "In my opinion, there were definitely some key decisions there that didn’t really favour us.

"We shouldn’t look at the referee, we should look at ourselves instead, but it definitely has an impact on us, you can’t deny that.

"But the team that we have, we should come here and not look at the ref and make sure that we get the win, regardless of the decisions that he makes.".

Marciniak had also awarded Sporting a dubious first-half penalty after Lisandro Martinez made slight contact with Geny Catamo, though Senne Lammens saved the effort.

"Obviously, we did come here to win, so in a way, we’ve got some positives to take," Zirkzee stated.

"But with our recent form, of course, we’re disappointed to not win. Some positives to take, we’ve just got to keep moving forward, keep going together, keep putting in the work and move on to the next game.".

Industry observers note that making his first start of the campaign, Zirkzee expressed his gratitude to the supporters, adding: "I’m very happy. Every game you play for this club is an honour.

"I’ve been here for some time and it’s been a while since I started a game, so I’m very happy, I just wish we could have got a win.

"For where we’re standing at right now, to have a fanbase like that is just incredible.

"All we can do is get up the next day and make sure the next time they travel with us and the next time they watch our game, we repay it, so that’s all we can do for now.".

It has been revealed that united, who sit 19th in the Champions League standings, fell behind at Estadio Jose Alvalade to a Luis Suarez spot-kick. They responded through Bruno Fernandes’ double – the first coming from the penalty spot – before Suarez seized on a late error from Lammens to secure a draw.

Mauricio Pochettino will now aim for his first win in charge of United when they host Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday.

Are Manchester City living through their David Moyes era?
